task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of September 8, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style reported feature about the small credit book at Alder Rill Village Stores and the tension between helping neighbors bridge payday and keeping stock on the shelves.

facts.text: An August 2026 business record shows Alder Rill Village Stores with 18 open household credit accounts alongside ordinary cash and card sales.
Owners Ceri and Olan Drel bought the shop in June 2025 and chose to continue a small-credit practice used by the previous owner.
The current rule limits a household's outstanding balance to $35 and charges no interest.
At August 31, 2026, the 18 open accounts had a combined $420 outstanding.
That balance is money owed to the shop, not a measured loss or cash available to pay a wholesaler.
The owners ask households to agree a repayment date, commonly their next payday, rather than offering an unlimited running balance.
Credit is restricted to ordinary food and household essentials under the shop's own policy.
Under the wholesaler's supplied agreement, the shop must pay within 21 calendar days of the wholesale invoice date, regardless of when households settle their accounts.
The owners do not publish customer names or individual balances on the shop noticeboard.
Customer Nessa Vale says her weekly wages sometimes arrive after the delivery day for the household items she needs.
Vale said, "It is a few days between the cupboard and payday, not a different kind of shopping list."
The reporting record includes no claim that all households using credit have the same income or reason for doing so.
Ceri Drel records repayments separately from new sales so she does not count the same goods as sold twice.
Drel said, "Being paid on Friday does not make Tuesday's milk a second sale."
Two of those 18 accounts are temporarily blocked from taking further credit while repayments are arranged; their holders are not identified in the record.
They have not supplied a full annual bad-debt figure or a comparison proving credit increases the shop's profit.
The next full-service grocery store is nine miles away, although some households use delivery services.
A reduced-price shelf for near-date goods is available to all customers, not only those with credit accounts.
The shop retains a counter drawer used by a former village postal agency that closed before the Drels arrived.
The owners have not proposed becoming a bank, adding interest charges or expanding the $35 limit.

forbidden_additions: The $420 is a confirmed loss, a fresh cash receipt or a second sale on repayment
Identifiable private account details, unlimited credit or proven profitability from the practice
